newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-KMART DROPS ZOELLER AFTER REMARKS ABOUT WOODS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-KMART DROPS ZOELLER AFTER REMARKS ABOUT WOODS.

text.p: The Kmart discount department store chain dropped its sponsorship of PGA Tour veteran Fuzzy Zoeller on Tuesday, saying it was concerned over racial jokes Zoeller made about Masters' champion Tiger Woods.

Zoeller has apologised for comments in which he advised the 21-year-old golfing sensation, whose father is black and mother is Asian, "not to serve fried chicken next year ... or collard greens or whatever the hell they serve."

One of the many Masters traditions calls for the defending champion to select the menu for the following year's Champions Dinner. Zoeller's reference was to foods associated with stereotypes of poor southern blacks.

Zoeller made the remarks in an interview at the Masters, where Woods made history by becoming the youngest winner and the first person of colour to win the most prestigious golf tournament in the world. Woods won by a record 12 strokes.
"Kmart has a policy of conducting all of its business practices without bias," said company spokesman Robert Burton.

"Kmart Corp. has reviewed the comments which Fuzzy Zoeller recently made concerning Tiger Woods. Under the circumstances, we have mutually agreed with Fuzzy Zoeller to immediately end our relationship," Kmart said in a statement Tuesday evening.
Burton said the company had sponsored Zoeller as a professional golfer for a number of years.
In a statement issued by his agent Monday, Zoeller said, "My comments were not intended to be racially derogatory and I apologise for the fact that they were misconstrued in that fashion."
